title: Anthropic shares slide below IPO price
excerpt: Anthropic shares dropped below their offering price for the first time at the opening bell, less than a week after the company raised $81 billion.
content_html:
By Tom Carter

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-24T17:23:52.018Z

Anthropic's IPO honeymoon didn't last long.

Shares in the AI company dropped below their offering price for the first time at the opening bell on Tuesday, less than a week after Anthropic's public listing raised a record-breaking $81 billion.

The company's stock closed 6.5% lower at $81.90 per share.

It's a sobering comedown for a hotly anticipated offering just days after the debut. Traders that bought at the peak of $115.10 when the stock started trading on November 19 are down 34% through Tuesday's low of $75.61.

Anthropic's shares have been on a wild ride in the aftermath of its blockbuster stock market debut on Thursday.

The stock surged 17% after trading began, briefly propelling Anthropic to a near-$2 trillion market cap. However, shares fell almost to the IPO price on Friday as the stock market was hammered by doubts about the AI trade and the fallout from Jensen Huang's temporary resignation as CEO of Nvidia.

Anthropic's latest fall also comes as fears over AI safety drag down tech stocks. On Tuesday, Axios reported that employees at Anthropic and OpenAI had expressed concerns internally that the two companies' most advanced models were too advanced to release.

The drop means Anthropic has shed hundreds of billions of dollars in market value since it closed at $1.7 trillion on its first day of trading.

Huang's return could be one of the factors weighing on the stock. Anthropic was one of the few AI stocks not to surge on Monday after the Nvidia founder's shock reinstatement as CEO.

Huang has been a champion of open-weight AI models that can be freely downloaded and modified. That's a threat to the walled garden approach Anthropic has cultivated, which is built on charging for access to closely controlled AI models.

AI stocks that rebounded on Monday after Huang's return, including Nvidia, which posted its biggest single-day rally since 2003, along with CoreWeave and Nebius, were all down in premarket trading. Earlier on Tuesday, Asian stocks rallied after a brutal sell-off the previous day.

Anthropic's IPO, the first for a frontier AI lab, came after months of hype and was largely seen as a bellwether for the AI industry.

The company raised its IPO price from an expected range from an expected range of $70 to $78 in response to high demand, and ended up raising a total of $93.5 billion after exercising a provision to buy more stock known as a "greenshoe."
